title: Quick-OOM eligibility requires a recent termination
answers: Why does VPA InPlace keep forcing updates after an old OOM?
When should an OOM bypass normal pod update eligibility checks?
How should the VPA updater distinguish stale and recent quick OOMs?
body:
Symptom: VPA InPlace repeatedly treats a days-old, short-lived container OOM as a fresh quick OOM on updater cycles.
Root cause: vertical-pod-autoscaler/pkg/updater/priority/update_priority_calculator.go:UpdatePriorityCalculator.AddPod inspected LastTerminationState for OOMKilled and short runtime without checking termination age; InPlace preserves that state.
Fix pattern: Require both FinishedAt minus StartedAt and the supplied now minus FinishedAt to be strictly less than EvictAfterOOMThreshold before granting quick-OOM eligibility; reuse the existing threshold.
Constraints: Applies to the quick-OOM eligibility path in all update modes. A stale OOM must fall through ordinary update eligibility checks, which may still permit an update; Recreate eviction already clears the retained termination state.
applies: VPA updater priority calculation, especially quick-OOM handling for pods using updateMode: InPlace.
